newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand's Chavalit has hard time securing support.
newsitem.headline: Thailand's Chavalit has hard time securing support.

text.p: Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, widely tipped to succeed Thailand's outgoing prime minister, faced problems on Thursday securing support from all factions in the ruling coalition, politicians said.
Time was closing in on him with premier Banharn Silpa-archa due to resign by Saturday after having been forced to declare his departure by key allies last weekend.
Chavalit, leader of the New Aspiration Party (NAP), the second largest member of Banharn's six-party administration, had support from some coalition partners, they said.
But he critically needed more substantive backing from the premier's own core Chart Thai party to be able to get the post, coalition sources said.
Chart Thai controls 91 of the 209 seats the coalition holds in the 391-seat parliament. Chavalit's NAP has only 57.

Key Chart Thai members of parliament, many of whom accused Chavalit of betraying Banharn, and MPs of two other smaller coalition parties -- the Prachakorn Thai and Social Action Party -- have not yet declared support for Chavalit, the sources said.

Parliament speaker Boon-ua Prasertsuwan said he had sent out letters to leaders of all 11 political parties represented in parliament to send in their signatures in support of candidates for the premiership.
Chavalit needs the signatures of at least 197 MPS from within the coalition to support his bid to be premier.

If he tried to get the signatures of MPs from outside the coalition to back his bid some coalition partners could say it was counter to their original agreement, and the alliance might crumble, coalition sources said.
"The situation is very confused and it is not certain whether he (Chavalit) will be the choice to succeed Banharn," Atthasith Saphyasith, a senior NAP leader told reporters.
Man Pattanothai, a senior Chart Thai member, told reporters on Thursday that party members had agreed that Banharn would be succeeded by party elder Pramarn Adireksarn.
"At this moment I can say that many Chart Thai members want Pramarn to be the next prime minister," he said.
Decho Savananond, deputy leader of Prachakorn Thai party, which has close links with Banharn, also said Pramarn looked likely to be nominated for the top post.

"With 18 MPs from Prachakorn and 91 from Chart Thai, a total of 109 supporting Pramarn, Banharn can claim he is justified in proposing Pramarn for the prime ministership," he told reporters. The total of 109 MPs would make up more than half of the 209 MPs representing the coalition now.

Pramarn has expressed interest in the post but did not rule out on Thursday that the Chart Thai party might nominate ex-premier Chatichai Choonhavan, leader of the opposition Chart Pattana party, to be its candidate for the top post.
Chart Pattana, with 53 seats, could be invited to join the coalition to enable that, political sources said.
Coalition sources also hinted that Banharn could as a last resort cite disagreement over a new premier's choice as an excuse to dissolve parliament and hold snap elections.

Chavalit, a former army commander in chief and a key player in Thai politics for decades both in and out of uniform, had been tipped in past years to be prime minister on several occasions but failed to make it to the top.
